summary.text: 妹 combines 女, which contributes a female-person category, with 未 as a sound element. Its common meaning is “younger sister.”

formation.text: 妹 is a phonosemantic compound: 女 contributes a female-person category, and 未 supplies a sound cue. This analysis is also applied to early forms.

components.text: 女 contributes the female-person category in 妹. No distinct earlier form or graphic change is specified.
未 is identified as the phonetic component. Separate Old Chinese reconstruction systems show a historical sound comparison with 妹; these forms are reconstructed rather than directly recorded.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Old Chinese system, 未 *mɯds and 妹 *mɯːds are similar reconstructed forms.
In the separate Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese system, 未 *m[ə]t-s and 妹 *C.mˤə[t]-s provide another comparison.

history.text: Forms are documented in oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and clerical scripts. These labels represent forms from different periods but do not by themselves establish a continuous sequence of graphic changes.
The traditional analysis identifies 未 as the sound element. An older explanation associated 妹 with 末, but the available evidence does not show that 未 arose through graphic corruption of 末.

uncertainties.text: Some oracle-bone uses and the bronze phrase 女妹辰 have been read as referring to 昧, “before daybreak.” Other readings include a place name, and the bronze phrase has also been interpreted as referring to childhood. These readings do not establish a semantic path to “younger sister.”

Reconstructions support a historical sound comparison between 未 and 妹, but ancient pronunciation was reconstructed rather than directly recorded; modern Mandarin readings alone do not prove the ancient relationship.
Comparative proposals linking 妹 to other language families are listed, but their evidence is not assessed here.

senses.period: attested in bronze inscriptions; exact date of the cited example unresolved
senses.text: A bronze inscription is read with the kinship sense “younger sister,” also given in the historical gloss 女弟. This does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning.

senses.period: oracle-bone and bronze inscription readings; phrase interpretation disputed
senses.text: Some early forms and a bronze phrase are interpreted as 妹 used to write 昧, “before daybreak” or “dawn twilight.” If this is a borrowing, the graph was reused for a different word because the words sounded alike or similar; the old word’s pronunciation and its relation to the kinship word are not established.

senses.gloss: younger female relative of the same generation
senses.text: Historical dictionary examples attest 妹 for a younger female relative of the same generation. The evidence does not date this sense or derive it from “younger sister.”
A broader use meaning “young woman” is attested, but its chronology and relation to the kinship sense are not established.

senses.gloss: modest first-person reference by a woman
senses.period: later literary use; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Historical examples attest 妹 as a woman’s modest first-person reference. The evidence does not establish when or how this usage developed.

limitations.text: The early readings do not establish whether the dawn-related use belonged to the same spoken word as the kinship sense or whether the graph was reused for a different word. If it was reused, the proposed mechanism is that the words sounded alike or similar; the old word’s pronunciation is not established here.
The broader and literary senses are attested, but the available examples do not establish their chronology or paths of development.

evidence.text: woman
Phonosemantic compound. 女 represents the meaning and 未 represents the sound.
女弟也。从女未聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *mɯːds): semantic 女 (“female, woman”) + phonetic 未 (OC *mɯds).
Probably Sino-Tibetan. Proposed etymologies:
* STEDT relates it to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *mi (“girl; female; feminine suffix”), whence Apatani nyimii (“girl; woman; female”), Proto-Loloish *C-mi² (“woman”), Proto-Karen *hmɨᴮ (“female; woman”).
* Schuessler (2007) compares it to Burmese မ (ma., “sister”) (whence အစ်မ (acma., “elder sister”), ညီမ (nyima., “younger sister”)), Miju ku-mai- (“woman”), Tibetan བུད་མེད (bud med, “woman”), and also Mizo hmei (“concubine”) (> Mizo hmei-chhia (“woman; wife”)), which STEDT relates to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *s-maj (“widow, widower”) instead.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Lexical Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解／甲金文字形與用例
evidence.text: The database analyzes the Shang oracle-bone and bronze forms as 女 semantic + 未 phonetic. It reports oracle-bone 妹 commonly used with the reading and sense of 昧, “before daybreak/dawn twilight”; bronze inscriptions use it for “younger sister” and also as a loan for 昧. Its examples include the Song gong Luan gui inscription “作其妹…媵簠” for the kinship sense, and the Da Yu ding phrase “女妹辰” read as 昧爽, dawn. The database then cites Shuowen’s 女弟 and the Odes’ 東宮之妹; it also notes the Yi’s broader 少女, “young woman,” usage. These are source interpretations and cited examples, not a secure chronology of the spoken senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 妹

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen gloss 女弟也 and analysis 从女，未聲, with fanqie 莫佩切. Its modern Mandarin reading is mèi. It separately glosses a younger female sibling, a younger woman of the same generation, a modest first-person address for a woman, and a young woman, citing classical and later literary examples. This supports attested extensions but does not establish when one sense developed from another.
evidence.title: A00902 妹 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The page reproduces “女弟也。从女未聲” and displays forms labeled oracle bone, Spring and Autumn bronze, Shuowen seal script, Western Han clerical script, and Eastern Han clerical script. Duan Yucai quotes the Odes gloss 女子後生曰妹 and notes competing old explanations: 釋名 associates 妹 with 昧, while 白虎通 explains it with 末. The source records historical wordplay/analysis, not conclusive derivation from either word.

These citations attest uses but do not establish the chronology or semantic path among them.
evidence.title: A00902 妹 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 大盂鼎 inscription text, Chinese Wikisource
evidence.text: The page labels the inscription as early Western Zhou and states that the vessel was cast in King Kang’s 23rd year. Its transcription has 女妹辰有大服; the edited text renders this 汝昧辰, while an annotation interprets 昧辰 as the owner’s childhood. Thus the page supplies a competing reading against the common dawn-twilight interpretation; it does not settle the disputed phrase on its own.
evidence.title: 大盂鼎銘文 — 維基文庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Lexical Database)
evidence.text: The entry shows oracle, bronze, and seal-script forms and analyzes the early graph as 女 semantic + 未 phonetic. It reports oracle-bone uses commonly read as 昧 ‘the time before daybreak’; bronze examples include 妹 meaning younger sister and a loan use for 昧. It cites the Song gong Luan gui and Da Yu ding. These are the database’s readings of the inscriptions, not a demonstrated chronology between the senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 妹

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen analysis 女弟也、从女未聲 and fanqie 莫佩切; it gives modern Mandarin mèi and records senses including younger sister, younger female relative of the same generation, modest first-person reference by a woman, and young woman. Its cited examples attest uses but do not establish when or how the senses developed.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The oracle-bone reading is unsettled: CUHK describes it as commonly meaning dawn twilight, while an Academia Sinica abstract records both place-name and 昧爽 interpretations. That abstract could not be opened, so the competing arguments and exact earliest contextual attestations remain unresolved.
No inscription image was visually inspected. CUHK cites named bronze vessels and gives inscription text, but this report relies on the lexicon’s transcription and interpretation.

The date of the Song gong Luan gui inscription was not independently verified from an excavated-object catalogue; Spring and Autumn bronze is the broad period label shown by Dong Chinese for a bronze form.

A chronological semantic path from dawn twilight to younger sister is not established. Bronze sources attest both uses, and later classical sources document kinship and broader young-woman senses, but no source here demonstrates the semantic transition.

The 《詩·衛風·碩人》 and 《易·歸妹》 examples are textually ancient, but this search did not verify their manuscript dates or establish that their preserved wording is the earliest attestation of the respective senses.

The claim that 未 and 妹 are phonologically related is supported by component analysis and reconstruction comparisons, but ancient readings are reconstructed rather than directly recorded; modern Mandarin is not independent proof of the ancient sound relation.
The local Baxter–Sagart rows were inspected and preserved exactly; the official external source page for the exact 未 row was not verified. The local file is not treated as an external source URL.
Unicode Unihan GetUnihanData pages for 妹, 未, and 女 could not be accessed; the current-reading cross-check with official records was therefore incomplete.

No reliable evidence was found to establish a graphic corruption from 未 to 末 in 妹. Duan Yucai notes an older 末-based explanation, while Shuowen and the inspected paleographic dictionary give 未 as the phonetic element; these positions should remain distinguished rather than treating corruption as demonstrated.
A recent paper reports traditional place-name versus dawn interpretations of oracle-bone 妹, but its page failed to open. Further source inspection is required before adjudicating the disagreement.
The Sino-Tibetan comparisons in the imported Wiktionary excerpt were not investigated in this bounded search; no external comparative etymology is asserted here.

The official Xiaoxuetang result did not load the requested 妹 query correctly; no record-specific glyph or rights notice could be verified there. Commons gives a Sinica record identifier for the oracle-form redraw, but this run did not independently inspect that exact record.
No physical oracle-bone or bronze inscription image was inspected. The selected Commons images are modern redrawings of script forms.
The bronze-file search result turned up a Commons page for 妹-bronze.svg, but opening it failed; its exact original image URL and licensing details were not verified, so it is omitted.

The Da Yu ding phrase 女妹辰 is interpreted differently: the inspected transcription normalizes it to 汝昧辰 and glosses it as the owner’s childhood, whereas the dossier’s CUHK reference reports a dawn-twilight reading. This run does not resolve the disagreement or establish a secure early dawn sense.

This response is limited to external evidence and candidate glyph sourcing. It does not independently revalidate the dossier’s component phonology or Unihan current-readings; official Unihan pages remained inaccessible.

No image selected: previously attempted oracle and seal images were reported as HTTP 404 and are excluded; the alternate Commons bronze redraw’s exact description page failed to open, leaving its direct URL and license unverified. CUHK’s linked oracle-form page also failed to load.

CUHK reads some oracle-bone 妹 forms as 昧 ‘before daybreak’ and the Da Yu ding bronze phrase 妹辰 as 昧爽, while the dossier records an alternative reading of that phrase as childhood. This pass did not resolve the inscription reading or establish a semantic chronology from dawn to younger sister.

The evidence reviewed supports the traditional 女 + 未 analysis and later senses, but this pass did not independently check the readings of both 未 and 妹 in the local Baxter–Sagart table or official Unihan records. Do not use current Mandarin pronunciation as proof of an ancient sound relationship.
No physical inscription image was inspected; the image candidate was described as a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: Early oracle-bone forms of 妹 have been interpreted as referring to dawn, but some readings identify a place name instead. The bronze phrase 女妹辰 also has competing interpretations, and the available evidence does not establish a chronological path between the disputed dawn reading and the kinship sense “younger sister.”
